identity.title: Observations of AGN-driven feedback: dynamics and ionization of the filaments in M87
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present a comprehensive kinematic and ionization analysis of the warm ionized filaments ($\sim$10$^4$ K) in M87, the central galaxy of the Virgo cluster, using new integral field spectroscopy from MEGARA (GTC) and SITELLE (CFHT).
Combined with archival ALMA, MUSE and *Chandra* data, these observations offer a multi-phase view of gas dynamics.

evidence.quote: We present a comprehensive kinematic and ionization analysis of the warm ionized filaments ($\sim$10$^4$ K) in M87, the central galaxy of the Virgo cluster, using new integral field spectroscopy from MEGARA (GTC) and SITELLE (CFHT).

For these observations, LR-R Volume-Phased Holographic (VPH, i.e., VPH675-LR) was used, covering 6096.5–7303.2 Å with a spectral resolution of $R \sim 6000$, corresponding to a velocity resolution of $\Delta v \sim$50 km s$^{-1}$.

provided.value: New imaging Fourier transform spectroscopy (SN1 and SN3 filters) mapping the full filamentary network (11' x 11' FOV).

SITELLE provides a 11$'$ $\times$ 11$'$ FOV, covering the entire filamentary network and its surroundings, with spatial sampling of 0.32$\ensuremath{''}$ per spaxel (cite: Drissen2019).

analysis_steps.goal: Reduce MEGARA and SITELLE optical IFU observations, subtract stellar continuum, and fit emission lines

method.value: Reduce MEGARA blocks with MEGARA DRP and custom sky/wavelength corrections; reduce SITELLE with ORBS/ORCS and Gaia DR3 flux calibration. Subtract stellar continuum using pPXF with MILES templates. Fit optical emission lines with 1 or 2 Gaussian components using LMFIT (for MEGARA) and ORCS (for SITELLE).

evidence.quote: Each observing block was reduced independently using the MEGARA Data Reduction Pipeline `MEGARA DRP` (version 0.15).
The median spectrum was fitted using pPXF algorithm (Penalized Pixel-Fitting; (cite: Cappellari2004)).

For each spectrum, the H$\alpha$, \[N II\]$\lambda$6548, 6583 and \[S II\]$\lambda$6716, 6731 lines were fitted simultaneously with Gaussian profiles using the `LMFIT` routine, based on the Levenberg-Marquardt least-squares algorithm (cite: Newville2016).

key_parameters.value: 0.31'' square spaxels for MEGARA; 0.32'' spaxels binned 2x2 for SITELLE

evidence.quote: Finally, each observing block was resampled onto a regularized grid with 0.31$\ensuremath{''}$ square spaxels, producing data cubes with dimension of 43 $\times$ 40 $\times$ 4300, corresponding to a total of 1720 spectra per cube.
To enhance the SNR, maps were spatially binned (2 $\times$ 2).

assumptions.value: Galactic extinction A_V = 0.063 mag, R_V = 3.1 following Cardelli et al. (1989); systemic velocity v = 1307 km s^-1

evidence.quote: Fluxes were corrected for Galactic extinction assuming $A_V = 0.063$ mag (NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database) and $R_V = 3.1$, following the (cite: Cardelli1989) extinction law, with a wavelength-dependent correction applied to each line.

For consistency with previous studies (cite: Werner2013; Simionescu2018), we adopt a systemic velocity of $v = 1307$ km s$^{-1}$ for M87 ($z = 0.00436$, $D_L = 16.1$ Mpc; (cite: Blakeslee2009)), where 1$'$ = 4.68 kpc.

fitting.value: Levenberg-Marquardt least-squares via LMFIT; 3-sigma residual criterion and AIC difference (Delta AIC > 10) for 2-component selection

evidence.quote: If $\epsilon_\text{line} > 3 \times \epsilon_c$ (following a $3\sigma$ criterion), the addition of a second component is considered.
In most cases, the two-component fits in the northwestern region are justified when the AIC difference, defined as $\Delta \text{AIC} = \text{AIC}_{N + 1} - \text{AIC}_N$, exceeds 10 (cite: Wei2016).

validation.value: Visual inspection of spectra and AIC statistical validation

evidence.quote: A visual inspection of the spectra was also performed to validate the statistical selection of components.

analysis_steps.goal: Model analytical thin-disk rotation and compute velocity structure functions (VSFs) and turbulent heating rate

method.value: Compare SITELLE velocities to an analytical thin-disk rotation model. Compute first-order VSFs across MEGARA, SITELLE, ALMA CO(2-1), and segmented MUSE subregions to extract slope, flattening scale, and amplitude. Estimate turbulent heating rate Q_turb and radiative cooling rate Q_cool in the FE filament.

key_parameters.value: Velocity uncertainty threshold <= 20 km s^-1; localized VSF aperture radius ~0.39 kpc spaced by ~100 pc

evidence.quote: To ensure the reliability of the VSFs, spaxels with velocity uncertainties greater than 20 km s$^{-1}$ were excluded, a threshold above the mean uncertainty that does not significantly affect the results.

analysis_steps.goal: Analyze optical emission line diagnostics and H\alpha - X-ray surface brightness correlation

method.value: Compute optical line ratios ([O I]/H\alpha, [N II]/H\alpha, [S II]/H\alpha, [S II]6716/6731), WHAN diagrams, and velocity dispersion vs. line ratio correlations. Decompose Chandra X-ray emission into 4 components using pGMCA and compare X-ray and SITELLE H\alpha surface brightness across filament regions.

evidence.quote: As a first step, we examine key emission-line ratios sensitive to ionization mechanisms such as shocks: \[O I\]/H$\alpha$, \[N II\]/H$\alpha$ and \[S II\]/H$\alpha$.

To further investigate the nature of the ionizing sources in the SE and FE filaments, we use the Width H$\alpha$-Nitrogen (WHAN) diagram (cite: CidFernandes2010; CidFernandes2011), traditionally used to classify galaxies by dominant ionization mechanisms.
We use deep archival *Chandra* observations of M87, from which the filamentary X-ray component is isolated using the Poisson Generalized Morphological Component Analysis (pGMCA; (cite: Bobin2020)).

key_parameters.value: 4 components in pGMCA decomposition; 1 kpc-wide concentric annuli for radial line ratio gradients

evidence.quote: Figure 8 presents these ratio maps along with radial gradients derived from SITELLE data, computed using concentric 1 kpc-wide annuli centered on the galaxy nucleus.
We decompose the X-ray emission into four components reflecting a mix of structures: diffuse halo, AGN cavities, and filaments – without a strict one-to-one association.

evidence.quote: Within each annulus, line ratio distributions are summarized with boxplots (median, interquartile range, and overall spread), and a weighted linear regression on median values to quantify the radial trends.

We constructed spaxel-by-spaxel diagrams of velocity dispersion versus \[N II\]/H$\alpha$ and \[S II\]/H$\alpha$ for each pointing and velocity component (where applicable), and quantified the trends using the Pearson correlation coefficient $r$.

claims.experiment: Compare SITELLE LOS velocity maps across the full filament network to an analytical thin-disk rotation model (i = 25 deg, PA = 45 deg) governed by the SMBH and stellar bulge potential.
claims.result: Outer filaments including the SE, FE, and horseshoe-like filaments exhibit substantial velocity residuals exceeding 100 km s^-1 relative to the disk model.
claims.finding: A simple rotating disk model is insufficient to explain the full range of filament motions in M87, which are shaped by local AGN feedback processes.

claims.hypothesis: The warm ionized gas and cold molecular gas in the SE filaments are kinematically coupled and share turbulent properties.
claims.experiment: Convolve MEGARA H\alpha maps to match the ALMA beam, resample ALMA CO(2-1) maps onto MEGARA's grid, and compare flux ratios, LOS velocities, velocity dispersions, and first-order VSFs.
claims.result: Emission peaks align closely, mean LOS velocity offset is (29 +/- 1) km s^-1, and both tracers show similar small-scale VSF slopes (~2/3), while H\alpha velocity dispersion is broader ((57 +/- 1) km s^-1 vs (26 +/- 2) km s^-1).
claims.finding: Ionized and molecular gas are largely co-spatial, kinematically aligned, and dynamically coupled on small scales, while broader ionized lines reflect a higher volume filling factor and multiple LOS components.

evidence.loc: Comparison Between SE Filaments and CO(2-1)
evidence.quote: The velocity-difference map reveals a strong correspondence across most of the overlapping region, with offsets typically below 55 km s$^{-1}$ and a mean of $(29 \pm 1)$ km s$^{-1}$. This supports the idea that ionized and molecular gas are largely co-spatial and kinematically aligned.

evidence.loc: Comparison Between SE Filaments and CO(2-1)
evidence.quote: On small scales, CO(2–1) and H$\alpha$ VSFs follow similar power-law trends with slopes close to 2/3.

evidence.loc: Comparison Between SE Filaments and CO(2-1)
evidence.quote: Despite the overall velocity alignment, the velocity dispersions differ: H$\alpha$ profiles are systematically broader than CO(2-1), with mean values of $(57 \pm 1)$ km s$^{-1}$ versus $(26 \pm 2)$ km s$^{-1}$, respectively.

claims.hypothesis: Turbulence across the filamentary network is driven by a common small-scale mechanism and turbulent dissipation balances radiative cooling in the outer FE filament.
claims.experiment: Compute localized first-order VSFs across MUSE, MEGARA, and SITELLE velocity maps and calculate the turbulent heating rate Q_turb at the seeing scale in the FE filament.
claims.result: VSFs show consistent steep slopes (> 2/3) and flattening at ~0.2-0.3 kpc (amplitudes ~30 km s^-1 in SE, ~15-20 km s^-1 in FE), though flattening in the SE filament disappears when isolating the primary velocity component; in the FE filament, Q_turb = 4.9e-28 erg s^-1 cm^-3 (~10% of Q_cool = 4.1e-27 erg s^-1 cm^-3).
claims.finding: Uniform small-scale VSF flattening may suggest energy injection from Type Ia supernovae, but interpretation is heavily limited by LOS superposition and finite aperture effects, and small-scale turbulent heating accounts for only ~10% of radiative cooling in the FE filament.

evidence.quote: Velocity structure functions (VSFs) of the warm and cold gas in the central and SE filaments show consistent steep slopes (> 2/3) and flattening on small scales of a few hundred parsecs, possibly suggesting energy injection from Type Ia supernovae, though interpretation is method-limited.

Interestingly, for the SE filaments, the VSF based on the first component does not exhibit a clear flattening; instead, the power increases steadily toward larger scales. This suggests that the flattening seen in the one component VSF may not correspond to a physical scale break, but rather the impact of LOS complexity.

why_this_data.value: MEGARA provides higher spectral resolution (R ~ 6000) targeting the SE filaments (overlapping the only known ALMA molecular clump) and the isolated FE filament outside the previous MUSE WFM FOV, while SITELLE maps the entire 11' x 11' filamentary network.

evidence.quote: In this context, we present new integral field spectroscopy of two key regions in M87’s filamentary nebula with MEGARA. The first targets the inner region ($\sim$3 kpc southeast of the nucleus) beyond the inner radio lobes and overleaping the only known molecular gas clump.

Both regions fall outside the previous MUSE wide field mode (WFM) pointing (1$\ensuremath{'}~\times~1\ensuremath{'}$). Complementary SITELLE imaging Fourier transform spectroscopy provides full mapping of the ionized gas across the network.

why_this_method.value: First-order VSFs quantify velocity variations across spatial scales to probe turbulent driving; WHAN diagrams classify ionization when [O III]5007 and H\beta are outside spectral coverage; pGMCA isolates morphologically distinct X-ray filament emission without prior physical assumptions.

evidence.quote: VSFs are typically expressed as a function of the scalar separation $l = |\mathbf{l}|$, providing a statistical description of velocity variations across spatial scales.

It an alternative to the classical Baldwin, Phillips & Terlevich (BPT) diagram (cite: Baldwin1981) when key emission lines such as \[O III\]$\lambda$5007 and H$\beta$ are unavailable, as in our MEGARA and SITELLE data.
The pGMCA method can extract a user-defined number of components with no prior physical or instrumental knowledge, by focusing on the morphological diversity of the different emissions.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Three-component Gaussian emission line fits were tested for MEGARA spectra but never statistically required.

evidence.quote: A third component was also tested but never required.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Standard single mean sky spectrum subtraction in MEGARA DRP was replaced with subtracting the mean of the two nearest sky fiber groups due to strong sky residuals.

evidence.quote: Instead of subtracting a single mean sky spectrum from all fibers, we subtracted the mean of the spectra from the two nearest sky fiber groups for each fiber within the pseudo-slit.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Classical BPT ionization diagnostics and [O II] electron density diagnostics were not used because H\beta and [O III]5007 are outside SITELLE/MEGARA coverage and the [O II] doublet has low SNR and is unresolved in SITELLE SN1.

evidence.quote: Combined with the unresolved doublet in SN1 data, this prevents the use of \[O II\] for reliable electron density diagnostics. H$\beta$ and \[O III\]$\lambda$5007 are outside the SITELLE filter coverage, further limiting ionization diagnostics.

limitations_admitted.value: VSF measurements are affected by LOS projection effects and unresolved kinematic substructure, which can create artificial flattenings (as demonstrated when comparing 1-component and 2-component fits in the SE filament).

evidence.quote: Our results in the SE filaments (Section 3.2.1) support this: approximately 23% of spaxels exhibit multiple velocity components, and the $\sim$0.3 kpc flattening vanishes when the VSF is computed using only the first component.

limitations_admitted.value: Atmospheric seeing suppresses VSF power and steepens slopes at small scales, making VSFs unreliable below the seeing limit.

evidence.quote: Therefore, we consider the VSFs unreliable below the seeing limit.

limitations_admitted.value: Finite window/aperture sizes and reduced pair statistics at large separations can introduce geometric distortions or artificial flattenings in VSFs.

evidence.quote: This suggests the flattening may partly reflect a geometric distortion related to the filament’s cross-section within the aperture, rather than a genuine physical dissipation scale.

limitations_admitted.value: Increased noise and lower spectral resolution in SITELLE systematically elevate VSF amplitudes and prevent reliable velocity dispersion analysis.

evidence.quote: Given these limits, velocity-dispersion results are not used in our analysis, though the map is provided for reference in Appendix 8.
This may partly explain the systematically higher VSF amplitudes seen in SITELLE, likely driven by increased noise and its lower spectral resolution.

limitations_admitted.value: Segmentation of MUSE filaments into subregions is visual and subjective, with ambiguity at filament junctions.

evidence.quote: The segmentation is inherently subjective, relying on visual identification of morphological and kinematic continuity in projection.

limitations_admitted.value: Turbulent heating rate estimates assume perfect small-scale kinematic coupling between cool filaments and the hot ICM plasma, which cannot yet be verified with current X-ray spatial resolution.

evidence.loc: Turbulent Heating in the FE filament
evidence.quote: We note that our estimated turbulent heating rate relies on the assumption that the kinematics of cool filaments and hot plasma are perfected coupled on small scales, which cannot be verified with existing X-ray telescopes yet due to their limited spatial resolution.

limitations_admitted.value: Spaxel-level WHAN diagnostics are sensitive to H\alpha SNR and stellar continuum dilution.

evidence.quote: To assess measurement impact, we examined $W_\alpha$ versus H$\alpha$ SNR, finding strong positive correlations (Pearson coefficients 0.93 for SE, 0.76 for FE). This sensitivity highlights limitations of spaxel-level WHAN diagnostics and suggests integrated-region analyses yield more reliable ionization classifications.

limitations_admitted.value: The pGMCA algorithm may struggle to isolate small, low-surface-brightness clumps like the FE filament compared to extended structures.

evidence.quote: Alternatively, the observed discrepancy may reflect limitations in isolating diffuse filamentary X-ray emission using pGMCA: as the algorithm can extract components based on their morphological features, it will more easily retrieve sources that are extended with a characteristic shape than small clumps – particularly in low surface brightness regions.

referee_caveats_inferred: The claim of Type Ia supernovae driving turbulence at ~100-300 pc scales is weakened by the disappearance of the VSF flattening in the SE filament once the two LOS velocity components are separated.
The ALMA CO(2-1) comparison relies entirely on pre-existing masked moment maps from Simionescu et al. (2018) rather than joint spectral fitting of the CO cube.
